# Exact product-base capacity for convex continuation of a source weight

This note tests the denominator cost of continuing the new own-fiber
projective boundary weight to a globally convex physical potential.
It gives an exact obstruction to a denominator-only parity estimate.
It does not discard cap credits on the additionally weighted fibers.

## 1. A barycentric product forces its full multiplicity cost

Let P be a finite set of distinct integer bases, N=|P|, and suppose its
arithmetic centroid p=N^(-1)sum_(z in P)z belongs to P. Let every fiber
be the same convex body K. Let phi(n,x) be a finite nonnegative function,
convex in x for each fixed boundary normal n, with finite positive own
boundary cost

    D=integral_(boundary K) phi(n_K(x),x)dH_(d-1)(x).

This includes the projective boundary weight for any interior source of
K. Consider ANY finite nonnegative continuation Psi(n,z,x), convex in
the joint physical variables (z,x) for each n, satisfying

    Psi(n,p,x)>=phi(n,x)

on the actual own-fiber boundary. Its total boundary cost obeys

    sum_(z in P) integral_(boundary K) Psi(n_K(x),z,x)dH_(d-1)(x)
       >= N D.                                             (1)

Proof: for each fixed boundary point x and its normal n, convexity at
(p,x)=N^(-1)sum_z(z,x) gives sum_z Psi(n,z,x)>=N phi(n,x).
Integrate this pointwise inequality. The z-independent continuation
Psi(n,z,x)=phi(n,x) is admissible and attains equality when phi is defined
convexly on all continuous space, as the projective tangent extension is.
Thus the exact minimum cost is N D, not merely a lower estimate.

On the genuine R4 product this gives31D, whereas the integer parity
budget is4. Already for n=1 and P={-m,...,m}, the exact factor is2m+1,
unbounded at fixed n. Both are actual complete lattice bases of convex
products; no artificial gaps or detached point laws are being used.

This does NOT contradict the own-fiber Gamma payment. It proves that
the payment cannot be propagated by assuming a universally bounded
denominator while ignoring all cap credit of the additional fibers.

## 2. The opposite exposed-base case has exact cost one

Suppose instead p is an exposed vertex of conv P. Choose affine ell
with ell(p)=0 and ell(z)<0 at every other base. For a source potential
phi as above, assume it is uniformly bounded on the finite union of
the other actual boundary fibers and their normals. This holds for
the projective tangent-extended potential on compact convex fibers.
Then, for sufficiently large finite B,

    Psi(n,z,x)=[phi(n,x)+B ell(z)]_+

is convex in (z,x), equals phi at p, and vanishes on every other actual
boundary fiber. Its exact total cost is D, which is necessarily minimal
because the own fiber alone costs D. The same geometric construction
works for unequal other fibers; only boundedness is used.

Thus the continuation cost already distinguishes exposed bases from
barycentric ones. A center-selection or contact argument would have to
use that distinction quantitatively rather than assert a common factor.

## 3. An exact finite base invariant for constant-in-x source weights

For a general finite P and p in P, define

    T(P,p)=max {sum_z w_z:0<=w_z<=1,
                          sum_z w_z(z-p)=0}.                (2)

The maximum is attained on a compact polytope. Jensen with normalized
weights w_z/T and nonnegativity shows that any nonnegative convex g
on base space with g(p)>=1 has

    sum_z g(z)>=T(P,p).

The same pointwise argument gives total continuation cost at least
T(P,p)D for EVERY nonconstant source weight phi from Section1 as well:
apply Jensen at the same continuous boundary point using a maximizing w,
then integrate. This is a lower bound only. Multiplying a nonconstant
convex phi by a base hinge need not be jointly convex, so the sharp
attainment construction below is restricted to its stated constant-in-x
case (apart from the separately proved arithmetic-centroid and exposed
cases).

This is sharp. The finite hinge LP has the exact dual

    min_a sum_z [1+a dot(z-p)]_+ = T(P,p).                    (3)

Indeed write t_z>=0 and t_z>=1+a dot(z-p); its dual variables obey
exactly(2). Both sides are feasible with finite value, so finite LP
duality applies. Attainment of the primal can also be seen by eliminating
a: the projection onto t is a closed polyhedron, and its intersection
with any fixed objective sublevel is compact. A minimizing hinge g
therefore realizes the stated convex-extension minimum.

If the prescribed source weight phi(n,x)=h(n)>0 is independent of x,
the product-body continuation minimum is exactly T(P,p)D: the preceding
Jensen lower bound applies pointwise, while
Psi(n,z,x)=h(n)[1+a dot(z-p)]_+ attains it. In particular this applies
to the projective construction when the source is already the ordinary
centroid, so its projective parameter is zero and h=h_K.

For the arithmetic-centroid case, w_z=1 proves T=N. For an exposed p,
the exposing linear functional in the balance equation forces all
w_z=0 except possibly w_p, proving T=1. These are the two exact geometric
extremes above. Equation(3) is a finite capacity calculation, not an OC
bound and not a theorem that any actual critical menu supplies a base
with small T.
